links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM fracture detection responses across three repeated runs (Fleiss' kappa)
links.effect: Consistency was very good for ChatGPT-4o (κ = 0.69) and Gemini 2.0 (κ = 0.61), and good for Claude 3.5 (κ = 0.44).
links.quote: Response consistency was very good for ChatGPT-4o (κ = 0.69) and Gemini 2.0 (κ = 0.61), good for Claude 3.5 (κ = 0.44).

links.outcome: Sensitivity and specificity of LLMs as standalone diagnostic tools for supracondylar fractures
links.effect: Sensitivity was 68.4% (Gemini 2.0), 58.7% (Claude 3.5), and 19.3% (ChatGPT-4o); specificity was low (33.1-36.0%), giving many missed fractures and false positives.
links.quote: Current LLMs demonstrate limited capability as independent diagnostic tools for pediatric supracondylar humeral fractures.

screen.reason: The study benchmarks the diagnostic accuracy and consistency of three commercial multimodal LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, Claude 3.5) on pediatric elbow radiographs without testing any deployment practices or safeguards.
